name: Pro 3 | Work Order Emails to Jobber | Advanced

values.content:
You read one email sent to a trades company's shared inbox and pull out the work order.

Reply with JSON only, no prose and no code fences, using exactly these keys:
{"title":"","client_name":"","client_company":"","client_email":"","client_phone":"","site_address":"","work_overview":"","urgency":"","requested_date":"","notes":""}

Rules:
- Use "" for anything the email does not tell you. Never use null. Never guess.
- Copy emails, phone numbers and addresses character for character from the email. If it is not written in the email, leave it empty. Inventing one is worse than leaving it blank.
- title: a short line an office manager would recognise on a job list, under 80 characters. Describe the work, not the email ("No hot water, boiler fault F28" rather than "Re: urgent").
- client_name is the person. client_company is their business, if any.
- site_address is where the work happens, which may differ from any billing address.
- work_overview: what needs doing, what is broken, what access or timing constraints are mentioned. Plain sentences. Do not add anything the email does not say.
- urgency: one of emergency, urgent, normal, low. Judge it from the email's own words.
- requested_date: YYYY-MM-DD only if the email names a date. Leave empty for "as soon as possible".
- notes: anything a scheduler should know that does not fit above, or "".

parameters.content:
## Work order emails → Jobber
Every email in the shared inbox is read, checked, snapshotted as a PDF, and raised
in Jobber as a request against the right client. Attachments travel with it.

**Set up in this order**
1. Credentials: Gmail, OpenAI, Google Drive, Google Sheets, Pushover, and an
   **OAuth2 API** credential for Jobber (see the Jobber note on the right).
2. In Gmail create three labels: `WO-Processed`, `WO-Review`, `WO-Ignored`.
   Get their IDs with a one-off Gmail node (Resource: Label → Get Many) and paste
   them into **Config**. Label names will not work here, only IDs.
3. Create a Drive folder for the archive and a Google Sheet with a tab called
   **Work Orders**. Paste both IDs into Config.
4. The sheet's first row must be exactly these 21 headers, in this order:
   `logged_at, ref, status, title, client, company, email, phone, site_address,
   urgency, requested_date, from, subject, gmail_id, jobber_request_id,
   jobber_client_id, drive_folder, snapshot_pdf, attachments, flags, problem`
5. Activate. The trigger polls every minute and ignores anything already labelled.

## Nothing reaches the model unchecked
**Triage Email** reads the message whatever shape the Gmail node returns it in,
turns HTML into text, cuts quoted replies and signatures, and decides whether this
is a work order at all. Out-of-office replies, bounces and newsletters stop here
and cost nothing.

**Loop Over Items** processes one email at a time. That is what makes
`$('Node').first()` safe further down, and stops one email's attachments being
mixed with another's.

## The model reads, the code decides
**Validate Extraction** checks the model's answer against the email itself.
Any email address, phone number or postcode that is not in the original text is
removed and flagged. A client name the email never mentions is flagged. Missing
fields fall back to the subject line and the sender.

Nothing is ever blocked: a flagged work order still reaches Jobber, marked
NEEDS_REVIEW, labelled `WO-Review` and pushed to your phone.

## The PDF is built here, not bought
**Build PDF + Split Files** writes a real PDF in plain JavaScript, because an n8n
Code node cannot install a library. The snapshot keeps the full original email
including the quoted history, so the archive is complete even though the model
only ever saw the trimmed version.

Then it emits one item per file so Drive can upload them one at a time, and
**Collect Files** puts them back into a single item.

## Jobber
**Credential:** Type *OAuth2 API*, Grant Type *Authorization Code*.
Authorize URL `https://api.getjobber.com/api/oauth/authorize`
Access Token URL `https://api.getjobber.com/api/oauth/token`
Client ID/Secret come from your Jobber Developer Center app. Access tokens last
60 minutes; n8n refreshes them for you.

**Two things to check in GraphiQL once, against your API version:**
1. `clients(first: 5, searchTerm: "...")` — if `searchTerm` is not accepted on
   your version, the run still works: it flags CLIENT_SEARCH_UNSUPPORTED and
   creates the client, so watch for duplicates until you fix the argument name
   in **Build Jobber Documents**.
2. `requestCreate` — swap it for `jobCreate` in **Build Request Document** if you
   would rather skip the request stage and book work straight in.

Every mutation asks for `userErrors`, and **Check Result** treats a 200 with
errors as a failure, because Jobber returns 200 either way.

## Why the files go to Drive
Jobber's public API has no file upload mutation, so the PDF and the attachments
live in a Drive folder and the request in Jobber carries the link. If Jobber adds
an upload endpoint, only **Build Jobber Documents** needs to change.
